dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Provides many concrete thresholds and ordering (e.g., password length >=12, token validity ranges, pre‑check priority list) that a generic model would not enumerate, but most of the content restates official documentation rather than delivering brand‑new expert heuristics.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Encodes AWS‑specific workflow (pre‑flight checks, CONFIRM gate, snapshot before update, post‑verify steps). One point deducted because the procedure for update vs create is described only in prose, not as a distinct step‑by‑step checklist.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Contains a concrete NEVER list with specific security rationales and additional warnings throughout. Deducted one point for limiting the NEVER list to five items; more exhaustive anti‑patterns would be expected at expert level.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Front‑matter, description, when‑to‑use, activation triggers, and invocation schema are all present. Deducted one point because activation triggers are free‑form strings rather than a precise pattern or schema that guarantees reliable activation.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: The skill layers high‑level overview, quick navigation, and deep sections well, but the extensive CLI examples and full pre‑check tables appear early, adding cognitive load before the core concepts are introduced.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Destructive actions are gated by an explicit CONFIRM step and extensive pre‑checks, while creative configurations (e.g., custom attributes) are left flexible. One point deducted because delete operations are mentioned only in a generic warning, not with a dedicated safe‑delete procedure.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a recognizable structure (What it does, Mindset, Pre‑flight, Process, NEVER, Output contract) but the pattern is not named and mixes sections (e.g., QUICK REFERENCE inside the main body) making it slightly ad‑hoc.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Provides concrete CLI commands and a strict output contract, enabling an agent to execute the plan. However, the example outputs contain placeholders like <returned-id> that violate the ‘no placeholders’ rule, and update‑only flows (e.g., schema migration) are not fully detailed, leaving edge‑case gaps.
